candidates.title: Make your own integration services with Hyper-V sockets
candidates.reason: Review as current first-party evidence for the underlying non-network Hyper-V socket transport, Linux AF_VSOCK mapping, supported host families, Linux Integration Services, and required kernel options; it does not document hvc SSH as a supported end-to-end product workflow.

candidates.title: MSLab Linux preview and Hyper-V socket provisioning
candidates.reason: Review as Microsoft-owned, explicitly experimental lab evidence that MSLab provisions Linux guests through hv_socket and points to its Packer templates; do not treat a lab repository as a supported product contract.

candidates.title: MSLab Debian 11 SSH Direct Packer template
candidates.reason: Review as Microsoft-owned implementation evidence for a Debian 11 guest: OpenSSH socket activation on vsock port 22, the hv_sock module, and hostname-resolution handling. Validate current distribution applicability before reuse.

candidates.title: Windows Server 2019 Inside Out sample
candidates.reason: Review the Microsoft Press example of hvc.exe ssh from a Hyper-V host after installing Linux virtualization extensions and an SSH server; it is useful corroboration but is tied to Windows Server 2019-era material.

candidates.title: Hyper-V Socket Support for the built-in hvc.exe SSH command
candidates.reason: Review as community-authored diagnostic evidence in a Microsoft-owned repository. It traces hvc.exe through OpenSSH and hvc.exe nc over a Hyper-V socket, but the open feature request is not formal support documentation.

candidates.title: HVC - SSH Direct for Linux VMs on Hyper-V
candidates.reason: Review as named-expert historical evidence for the hvc ssh command and intended VMBus path. Retain the article's preview-era date and its comments reporting configuration-sensitive behavior.

candidates.title: Ubuntu hv_sock OpenSSH socket-activation regression
candidates.reason: Review as current distribution evidence that hvc.exe connectivity worked on Ubuntu 22.04 but failed on 24.04 when a required OpenSSH socket-activation unit was removed; use it to teach version validation rather than a universal recipe.

candidates.title: Virtualizing Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 on Hyper-V
candidates.reason: Review as historical Red Hat evidence that RHEL includes Hyper-V integration and VMBus drivers. It predates the current SSH Direct objective and does not document hv_sock, VSOCK SSH activation, hvc.exe, or a current support matrix.

candidates.title: RHEL 8.5 release notes: socat AF_VSOCK support
candidates.reason: Review as Red Hat evidence that its socat package supports AF_VSOCK listen and connect addresses. This is a useful diagnostic or relay building block, not evidence that RHEL supports Hyper-V SSH Direct end to end.

candidates.title: RHEL 10.2 AF_VSOCK namespace parameters
candidates.reason: Review as current Red Hat kernel evidence for AF_VSOCK behavior and namespace boundaries. It does not identify Hyper-V transport packaging, configure OpenSSH, or establish hvc.exe interoperability.

candidates.title: CentOS Stream 9 kernel modules include hv_sock
candidates.reason: Review as exact third-party package-index evidence that one CentOS Stream 9 kernel-modules-core build contains hv_sock. Confirm against the installed signed package; CentOS Stream is not interchangeable with RHEL and module presence does not prove SSH Direct.

candidates.title: Fedora 44 OpenSSH server package inventory
candidates.reason: Review as Fedora-owned evidence that the OpenSSH server package ships sshd.socket and sshd@.service components. The inventory does not prove a VSOCK listener, Hyper-V transport, or equivalent RHEL packaging.

candidates.title: Fedora 44 SELinux policy SSHD VSOCK rules
candidates.reason: Review as Fedora-owned evidence that current SELinux policy explicitly handles SSHD VSOCK sockets. It strengthens the generic composition but is neither a RHEL support statement nor an hvc.exe validation.

candidates.title: SUSE 16 kernel package hv_sock maintenance
candidates.reason: Review as current SUSE package evidence that hv_sock is actively carried and maintained. A changelog entry does not establish which SLES editions support SSH Direct or whether an SSH VSOCK listener is installed.

candidates.title: openSUSE Factory OpenSSH VSOCK listener packaging change
candidates.reason: Review as an archived openSUSE Factory package change describing socket-activated SSHD and a VSOCK listener. Its documented path targets libvirt and requires additional packages, so Hyper-V and SLES applicability remain unverified.

candidates.title: SUSE Package Hub virtme SSH-over-VSOCK history
candidates.reason: Review as SUSE package evidence that SSH-over-VSOCK is a maintained guest-management pattern. The package targets virtme/KVM workflows and does not prove Hyper-V hvc.exe compatibility.

candidates.title: Oracle Linux VSOCK interface configuration
candidates.reason: Review as current Oracle documentation for generic VSOCK configuration. It targets Oracle Linux KVM, not Oracle Linux as a Hyper-V guest; UEK and RHCK need separate Hyper-V and hvc.exe validation.

candidates.title: Linux Integration Services 4.1 Hyper-V sockets guide
candidates.reason: Review as historical Microsoft evidence that RHEL/CentOS and Oracle Linux with RHCK could load hv_sock for Hyper-V sockets. It is an old LIS 4.1 guide, does not configure SSH, and cannot establish current distro or Windows Server support.

candidates.title: systemd VM interface: automatic SSH on AF_VSOCK
candidates.reason: Review as maintained upstream evidence that systemd 256 and later can bind SSH to AF_VSOCK port 22 in a VM. Confirm each distribution ships and enables the generator; upstream behavior does not prove Hyper-V hvc.exe interoperability.

candidates.title: libvirt SSH proxy over VSOCK
candidates.reason: Review as maintained upstream implementation guidance for SSH socket activation on vsock port 22 and its alternatives. It provides a useful cross-distribution model but targets libvirt rather than Hyper-V SSH Direct.
